title: Bypass
statement: . Esto solo puede pasar por razones que están en la ley, y el condado debe probar una de ellas con pruebas fuertes. Ejemplos: daño físico grave a un niño. O uso fuerte de drogas o alcohol por mucho tiempo, cuando el padre también se resistió al tratamiento ordenado por la corte en los últimos 3 años. O el padre perdió los servicios para un hermano del niño y desde entonces no ha hecho un esfuerzo real por arreglar el problema.
source_says: when the court finds, by clear and convincing evidence, any of the following ... resisted prior court-ordered treatment for this problem during a three-year period
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT on glossary_terms id d249dad1. Searched 'WIC 361.5 reunification services need not be provided clear and convincing evidence', opened the public.law page twice. Read (b) opening line (clear and convincing evidence), (b)(6) 'infliction of severe physical harm to the child' plus finding it 'would not benefit the child', (b)(10) 'has not subsequently made a reasonable effort to treat the problems that led to removal', (b)(13) chronic drug or alcohol use plus resisted treatment. Note: the statute counts the 3 years back from the filing of the petition, and (b)(6) also needs a finding that services would not benefit the child; both are within what an 'example' can leave out.

title: AB 12
statement: The law that lets some youth stay in foster care until 21. You must be in foster care on your 18th birthday and meet other rules, like being in school or working.
source_name: CDSS Extended Foster Care (AB 12) page
source_says: To be eligible for EFC, youth must be age 18-21 and have had an order for foster care placement on their 18th birthday.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id 093c7b1d). Searched 'CDSS Extended Foster Care AB 12 eligibility order for foster care placement on 18th birthday', opened the CDSS page. It also lists the participation rules: high school, college or vocational school, 'Work at least 80 hours/month', job program, or medical condition.

title: Adoptive Parent
statement: En la mayoría de los casos, la adopción solo ocurre después de que terminan los derechos de los padres biológicos. Hay un tipo diferente: una adopción tribal tradicional para un niño indígena no termina los derechos de los padres biológicos.
source_says: Termination of parental rights is not required to effect the tribal customary adoption.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 4e5ae84b). Searched 'public.law WIC 366.24 tribal customary adoption', opened the public.law page, read (a)(1): tribal customary adoption 'means adoption by and through the tribal custom, traditions, or law of an Indian child's tribe.'

title: Active Efforts
statement: El nivel más alto de ayuda que el condado debe dar cuando el niño es un niño indígena según la ley. Eso quiere decir que el niño es miembro de una tribu, o que puede hacerse miembro y uno de sus padres biológicos es miembro.
source_says: any Indian tribe, band, nation, or other organized group or community of Indians recognized as eligible for the services provided to Indians by the Secretary
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id d05386cb). Searched '25 U.S.C. 1903 Indian child Indian tribe', opened the Cornell page. (4) says Indian child is 'any unmarried person who is under age eighteen and is either (a) a member of an Indian tribe or (b) is eligible for membership in an Indian tribe and is the biological child of a member'. (8) limits 'Indian tribe' to federally recognized tribes. Opened courts.ca.gov icwa-welfarecode.pdf (marked current as of September 2021): WIC 224.1(a) says the terms 'shall be defined as provided in Section 1903 of the federal Indian Child Welfare Act'; 224.1(b) adds unmarried 18 to 20 year olds in dependency; 306.6 lets a tribe without federal recognition take part but does not make ICWA apply. Opened courts.ca.gov icwa-active-efforts.pdf: 'Reasonable efforts are insufficient' supports 'higher level'. The entry says 'a tribe' with no limit, so a family from a tribe without federal recognition would read this as covering them. Could not open the current leginfo page for 224.1 (fetch failed).
fix: The higher level of help the county must give when the child is an Indian child under the law. That means the child is a member of a federally recognized tribe, or can become a member and has a birth parent who is a member.

title: Active Efforts
statement: The extra-hard work the county must do to keep a family together when the child is a member of a tribe, or can become one through a birth parent who is a member.
source_says: any Indian tribe, band, nation, or other organized group or community of Indians recognized as eligible for the services provided to Indians by the Secretary
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id d05386cb). Same sources as the definition record: Cornell 25 U.S.C. 1903(4) and (8), courts.ca.gov icwa-welfarecode.pdf (WIC 224.1(a), 306.6), courts.ca.gov icwa-active-efforts.pdf ('must provide active efforts to assist the Indian family in remaining together'). The simple line says 'a tribe' with no federal recognition limit.
fix: The extra-hard work the county must do to keep a family together when the child is a member of a federally recognized tribe, or can become one through a birth parent who is a member.

title: CFT
statement: Un grupo que se reúne para planear el cuidado de un niño. Incluye al niño, a la familia, a la persona que cuida al niño y a personas de apoyo. El equipo da ideas y consejos. La agencia del condado debe tomar en cuenta lo que dice el equipo, pero la agencia toma la decisión sobre la colocación.
source_says: Providing input into the placement decision made by the placing agency
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 13261386). Searched 'public.law WIC 16501 child and family team', opened WIC 16501: team is 'a group of individuals who are convened by the placing agency'; process 'shall engage the child or youth, the child's family, and other people important to the family'; members listed include 'The caregiver.' and 'The placing agency caseworker.' Opened WIC 16501.1 (https://california.public.law/codes/welfare_and_institutions_code_section_16501.1): (a)(3) 'The agency shall consider and document the recommendations of the child and family team'.

title: CFT
statement: A team of family and helpers who meet to plan how to care for a child. The team gives ideas, and the county agency makes the final placement choice.
source_says: Providing input into the placement decision made by the placing agency
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id 13261386). Same pages as the definition record: WIC 16501(a)(4) (team engages child, family, caregiver, caseworker; gives input into the placement decision made by the placing agency) and WIC 16501.1(a)(3) (agency shall consider and document the team's recommendations).

title: Continuance
statement: Un juez puede cambiar la fecha de una audiencia solo por una buena razón, y solo si el retraso no le hace daño al niño. Solo querer más tiempo no es suficiente. A veces la corte está muy ocupada y el juez escoge una nueva fecha.
source_name: WIC 352(a); Judicial Council booklet Juvenile Dependency Court and You
source_says: Continuances shall be granted only upon a showing of good cause ... a continuance shall not be granted that is contrary to the interest of the minor.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 45ba0c2f). Searched 'public.law WIC 352 continuance good cause', opened the page, read (a). It also says 'Neither a stipulation between counsel nor the convenience of the parties is in and of itself a good cause', which is the closest support for 'just wanting more time is not enough'. For the busy-court sentence opened the Judicial Council booklet (https://courts.ca.gov/sites/default/files/courts/default/2024-08/juvenile-dependency-court-and-you.pdf): 'the judge won't have time to give your case the attention it needs on the day you go to court' and 'This rescheduling is called a continuance.'

title: Chafee Grant
statement: entre los 16 y los 18 años de edad. Debe estar en la escuela por lo menos medio tiempo. El dinero es limitado, así que no todos los que lo solicitan lo reciben.
source_name: California Student Aid Commission, Chafee Grant site
source_says: Be enrolled in an eligible vocational school or college courses at least half-time. ... Funding is limited. ... Payment on an eligible California Chafee Grant Award is not guaranteed.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 63a7bfa7). Searched 'California Chafee Grant foster youth eligibility half time limited funding', csac.ca.gov/chafee would not load, opened chafee.csac.ca.gov. Also reads: 'Be a current or former foster youth who was a ward of the court, living in foster care, between the ages of 16 and 18' and 'Payments are made on a first-come first-served basis.' Side note outside this line: the same page says the state authorized '$4,500 annual award amounts for the 2025-26 academic year', while the entry's unchanged first sentence says up to $5,000.

title: Chafee Grant
statement: Es una beca. Pregunte en la oficina de ayuda financiera de su escuela qué pasa con el dinero si usted deja la escuela antes de tiempo.
source_name: California Student Aid Commission, Chafee Grant Frequently Asked Questions
source_says: If the student's status changes after funds are requested, please follow institution policy.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 63a7bfa7). Searched 'Chafee grant California Student Aid Commission half time 16 and 18', opened the CSAC FAQ PDF. It calls the award the California Chafee Grant, says to 'refer to the Chafee Payment Guide' for returning funds, and leaves a change in enrollment to school policy. It does not say the money never has to be returned, which matches the new wording.

title: Rehearing
statement: Cuando un árbitro judicial (referee) atiende su caso, normalmente usted puede pedir que un juez vuelva a ver el asunto. No puede pedirlo si el árbitro judicial actuaba como juez temporal, lo cual puede pasar cuando las partes están de acuerdo. Pregúntele a su abogado.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rules 5.542(a), 5.536(b); WIC 252
source_says: An application for a rehearing of a proceeding before a referee not acting as a temporary judge may be made by the child, parent, or guardian
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 98db1103). Searched 'rule 5.536 referee temporary judge stipulate; rule 5.542 rehearing', opened rule 5.542(a) (rehearing only where referee not acting as temporary judge, within 10 calendar days after service). Opened rule 5.536(b) (https://courts.ca.gov/cms/rules/index.cfm?linkid=rule5_536&title=five): 'the parties may stipulate under rule 2.816 that the referee is acting as a temporary judge with the same powers as a judge'. Opened WIC 252 on public.law: 'may apply to the juvenile court for a rehearing'.

title: .26 Hearing
statement: . Los papeles de la corte pueden mostrarla como .26 o 366.26. Algunas cortes la llaman audiencia de selección e implementación.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet Juvenile Dependency Court and You; San Diego Superior Court, Juvenile Court Dependency Hearings
source_says: What is a ".26" (two-six) hearing? ... .26 or 366.26
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 1d5824c4). Searched 'rule 5.725 selection of permanent plan 366.26 selection and implementation'. Opened rule 5.725 on courts.ca.gov (titled 'Selection of permanent plan', does not use 'selection and implementation'). Opened the booklet: says the hearing shows on court papers as '.26 or 366.26'. Searched '"selection and implementation hearing" 366.26 superior court', opened the San Diego Superior Court PDF (https://www.sdcourt.ca.gov/sites/default/files/sdcourt/juvenile3/juvenilefaq3/dependency_process.pdf): 'SELECTION AND IMPLEMENTATION HEARING: WIC §366.26, CRC 5.725-5.735.' Judicial Council bench card titles it '366.26 Hearing - Select and Implement Permanent Plan'.

title: CASA
statement: the judge appoints for a child.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.655(e)(1)
source_says: A CASA volunteer is a person who has been recruited, screened, selected, and trained ... has been appointed by the juvenile court as a sworn officer of the court
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 819fa466). Searched 'WIC 102 103 CASA appointed by judge; rule 5.655', opened rule 5.655 on courts.ca.gov. (e)(1) says the juvenile court appoints; (j) speaks of 'the appointment of CASA volunteers for children and nonminors'; no one-volunteer-per-child rule appears.

title: Disposition Hearing
statement: . El trabajador social escribe el plan de caso. En esta audiencia el juez revisa el plan y lo convierte en una orden de la corte.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.690(c); California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: the social worker must prepare a case plan. ... the court must consider the case plan and must find as follows:
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 741d9a7e). Searched 'rule 5.690 case plan social worker must prepare court must consider', opened rule 5.690(c): plan 'must be completed and filed with the court by the date of disposition'; court considers it and finds whether it 'meets the requirements of section 16501.1'. For 'makes it a court order' opened selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-parents: 'The judge will order you to complete all the reunification services.' Also WIC 361.5(a) on public.law: 'the juvenile court shall order the social worker to provide child welfare services'.

title: Foster Youth Bill of Rights
statement: enumera muchos de los derechos que tienen los niños y jóvenes en cuidado de crianza, incluido el derecho a estar seguros, ir a la escuela, ver a sus hermanos, tener privacidad, participar en actividades y mucho más. Los jóvenes también tienen otros derechos.
source_says: are not exhaustive of all rights set forth in the United States Constitution and the California Constitution
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id f384aa51). Searched 'public.law WIC 16001.9 foster youth rights not exhaustive', opened the page. (a) lists the rights named in the entry: 'To live in a safe, healthy, and comfortable home', 'To attend school', 'To visit and contact siblings', 'to maintain privacy', 'To participate in extracurricular ... activities'. (b) says the list is not exhaustive.

title: Initial Hearing
statement: Si sacaron a su hijo de su hogar y no se lo devolvieron, esta audiencia se debe hacer a más tardar al final del siguiente día hábil de la corte después de que se presenta la petición.
source_name: WIC 315
source_says: taken into custody under this article and not released to a parent or guardian ... not later than the expiration of the next judicial day after a petition
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id f69f2fb3). Searched 'public.law WIC 315 detention hearing next judicial day', opened the page and read the whole section. The Self-Help Guide for parents (cited by the entry) says 'This hearing must be held by the end of the day after the petition is filed.'

title: Extended Foster Care (EFC)
statement: . Los jóvenes pueden quedarse si están terminando la preparatoria (high school) o un programa parecido, están en la universidad o en capacitación laboral, trabajan por lo menos 80 horas al mes, están en un programa que les ayuda a conseguir trabajo, o no pueden hacer estas cosas por una condición médica.
source_says: The nonminor is employed for at least 80 hours per month. ... incapable of doing any of the activities described in paragraphs (1) to (4), inclusive ... due to a medical condition
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 355d8fda). Searched 'public.law WIC 11403 nonminor dependent 80 hours per month', opened the page. (b)(1) 'completing secondary education or a program leading to an equivalent credential', (2) 'postsecondary or vocational education', (3) 'program or activity designed to promote, or remove barriers to employment', (4) 80 hours, (5) medical condition. (a): 'eligible to receive support until they reach 21 years of age'. CDSS EFC page lists the same five.

title: Extended Foster Care (EFC)
statement: You can stay in foster care until 21 if you are in school or job training, work at least 80 hours a month, are in a job program, or cannot do these because of a medical condition. You sign an agreement to stay.
source_name: WIC 11403(b), (d); CDSS Extended Foster Care (AB 12) page
source_says: The youth must sign the Mutual Agreement for Extended Foster Care (form SOC 162) after turning age 18
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id 355d8fda). Opened the CDSS EFC page (five participation rules, 'Work at least 80 hours/month', 'remain in foster care until age 21', mutual agreement 'no later than six months after reaching age 18') and WIC 11403 on public.law ((b)(1)-(5); (d) 'both the youth and the agency ... have signed a mutual agreement'). The line says 'stay', which fits the CDSS rule that the youth 'have had an order for foster care placement on their 18th birthday'.

title: Minute Order
statement: Sacramento Superior Court, Dependency Court Terms; Santa Clara Superior Court, participants in dependency cases
source_name: Sacramento Superior Court, Dependency Court Terms; Santa Clara Superior Court, Participants in Dependency Cases
source_says: Document prepared by clerk recording orders of the court.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (source, id 2314cdfe). Searched 'Sacramento Superior Court juvenile dependency court terms minute order', opened the PDF, read the MINUTE ORDER entry; it supports both sentences of the definition. Searched 'Santa Clara Superior Court juvenile dependency participants minute order', opened https://santaclara.courts.ca.gov/divisions/juvenile-division/juvenile-dependency/participants-dependency-cases: 'The Clerk writes a summary of what happened in court and keeps the court files.' That page does not use the words 'minute order'; the Sacramento page carries the entry.

title: Non-Relative Extended Family Member (NREFM)
statement: Un amigo cercano de la familia es un ejemplo.
source_says: The parties may include relatives of the child, teachers, medical professionals, clergy, neighbors, and family friends.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 6a8bc7bd). Searched '362.7 nonrelative extended family member teachers, medical professionals, clergy, neighbors, and family friends', opened the public.law page and read the whole section. A family friend is one of several kinds of people listed, so 'one example' fits. NREFM is 'an adult caregiver who has an established familial relationship with a relative of the child ... or a familial or mentoring relationship with the child'.

title: Non-Relative Extended Family Member (NREFM)
statement: Un niño puede ser colocado con esta persona si el condado aprueba el hogar. Primero se considera a los parientes.
source_says: the home shall be evaluated, and approval of that home shall be granted or denied
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 6a8bc7bd). Opened WIC 362.7 on public.law (home of an NREFM must be evaluated and approved or denied under foster home standards). For 'relatives are looked at first' searched 'public.law WIC 361.3 preferential consideration relative', opened https://california.public.law/codes/ca_welf_and_inst_code_section_361.3: (a) 'preferential consideration shall be given to a request by a relative of the child'; (c)(1) 'the relative seeking placement shall be the first placement to be considered and investigated.'

title: Alleged Parent
statement: Hasta entonces, es posible que no tenga derecho a la custodia ni a los servicios de reunificación. Pregúntele a su abogado sobre las visitas.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, If you want to be included in your child's dependency case
source_says: You might not have the right to custody or reunification services.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id a4a70f07). Searched 'selfhelp.courts.ca.gov juvenile dependency alleged parent rights custody reunification services', opened the page. It says alleged parents 'have very few rights in dependency cases' and does not address visits for alleged parents, which fits 'Ask your lawyer about visits.'

title: Ombudsperson
statement: Los jóvenes de crianza pueden llamar o enviar un correo electrónico al Ombudsperson sobre cosas como maltrato, derechos que no se respetan o problemas con su colocación. La oficina mantiene su nombre en privado. Si alguien está en peligro, es posible que tenga que avisar a una agencia de protección de menores o de licencias, y hablará con usted sobre eso.
source_name: California Office of the Foster Care Ombudsperson, fosteryouthhelp.ca.gov
source_says: The law allows us to release certain information to certain people in the process of conducting our duties; however, if we need to share this information we will tell you.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id c47adf1a). Searched 'California Foster Care Ombudsperson confidentiality complaint', opened the home page twice and read the full answer under 'Is my call to the Ombudsperson's office confidential?'. Confirmed: 'We have a confidentiality policy to protect the identity of people who call to make a complaint'; 'If there is an immediate safety issue, we may also make a report to ... the county's Child Protective Services agency or the Community Care Licensing Division. If this happens, we will discuss this with you.' Youth can contact the office about 'issues related to foster youth rights, care, placement, and services'. The entry gives danger as the only time anything is shared; the office also says the law lets it share some information to do its work.
fix: Foster youth can call or email the Ombudsperson about things like mistreatment, rights not being respected, or problems with their placement. The office has a policy to protect your name. The law lets the office share some information to do its job, and it will tell you if it needs to. If someone is in danger right now, it may also report to child protective services or the licensing agency, and it will talk with you about that.

title: Ombudsperson
statement: La llamada es gratis.
source_name: California Office of the Foster Care Ombudsperson, fosteryouthhelp.ca.gov
source_says: toll free hotline
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id c47adf1a). Opened fosteryouthhelp.ca.gov; the page gives 1-877-846-1602 and calls it a 'toll free hotline'. The number matches the entry.

title: Ombudsperson
statement: They keep your name private, but if someone is in danger they may have to tell people who can help.
source_name: California Office of the Foster Care Ombudsperson, fosteryouthhelp.ca.gov
source_says: The law allows us to release certain information to certain people in the process of conducting our duties; however, if we need to share this information we will tell you.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id c47adf1a). Same page and same answer as the definition record. The danger part is confirmed ('If there is an immediate safety issue, we may also make a report to the appropriate agencies'). The simple line leaves out that the office may also share some information to do its work and will tell the youth first.
fix: They have a policy to protect your name. If they need to share what you said, they will tell you. If someone is in danger right now, they may report it to people who can help.

title: Witness
statement: cada lado puede traer testigos. Su abogado también puede hacerles preguntas a los testigos del condado.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(g)(1)
source_says: The right to confront and cross-examine the persons who prepared reports or documents ... The right to use the process of the court to bring in witnesses
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 6b44984b). Searched for WIC 316.1 mailing address, which returned rule 5.534; opened it and read (g) Advisement of hearing rights: (B) cross-examine report writers 'and the witnesses called to testify at the hearing', (C) bring in witnesses, (D) 'The right to present evidence to the court.' Booklet: 'the judge will have a trial to review evidence and listen to witnesses'.

title: Witness
statement: Judicial Council, Juvenile Dependency Court and You; Evidence Code §§700, 710; Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(g)
source_name: Evidence Code 700, 710; Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(g); Judicial Council booklet
source_says: Every witness before testifying shall take an oath or make an affirmation or declaration in the form provided by law
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (source, id 6b44984b). Searched 'public.law Evidence Code section 700; section 710 oath', opened both. 700: 'every person, irrespective of age, is qualified to be a witness'. 710 adds that a child under 10 'may be required only to promise to tell the truth.' Opened rule 5.534 on courts.ca.gov: subdivision (g) is 'Advisement of hearing rights' and holds the cross-examine and bring-in-witnesses rights, so the (g) letter is right. Opened the booklet: 'sometimes witnesses will testify.' Each cited source supports part of the entry.

title: Minor's Counsel
statement: WIC §317; California Courts Self-Help Guide for children and youth; Judicial Council, Juvenile Dependency Court and You
source_name: WIC 317(c)(1), (e), (f); California Courts Self-Help Guide for children and youth; Judicial Council booklet
source_says: the court shall appoint counsel for the child or nonminor dependent, unless the court finds that the child or nonminor dependent would not benefit from the appointment of counsel.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (source, id a882de1d). Searched 'WIC 317 shall appoint counsel for the child unless would not benefit', opened public.law WIC 317: (e) 'representation of the child's interests' and 'shall advise the court of the child's wishes'; (f) child's privilege. Searched and opened https://www.selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-children: 'your lawyer must tell the judge what is in your best interests and what you want'; 'your lawyer cannot tell anyone else what you have told them unless you say it is okay.' Opened the booklet: parents may 'ask your social worker or your child's lawyer for the information you need.' Each cited source supports part of the entry.

title: Commissioner
statement: En la corte de dependencia, un comisionado puede dirigir sus audiencias y dar órdenes. Un comisionado tiene todo el poder de un juez cuando las personas del caso están de acuerdo. Si usted no estuvo de acuerdo, es posible que pueda pedirle a un juez que revise la decisión. El plazo es corto, así que pregúntele a su abogado de inmediato.
source_name: Cal. Const., art. VI, §§ 21, 22; Cal. Rules of Court, rules 5.536(b), 5.542(a); WIC 252; L.A. Superior Court Local Rule 7.15
source_says: If there is a stipulation authorizing a commissioner or referee to sit as temporary judge, no rehearing right is available.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id d22cf708). Searched 'California Constitution article VI section 21 temporary judge; section 22 commissioners', opened Justia art. VI §21 ('On stipulation of the parties litigant the court may order a cause to be tried by a temporary judge') and §22 ('officers such as commissioners to perform subordinate judicial duties'). Opened rule 5.536(b) and rule 5.542(a) on courts.ca.gov (rehearing 'before the expiration of 10 calendar days after service'). Searched 'juvenile dependency court commissioner temporary judge stipulation rehearing', opened L.A. Superior Court Chapter 7 rules: rule 7.15 applies 'to referees and commissioners sitting in juvenile proceedings' and lets 'a child, parent, legal guardian, or DCFS' apply for rehearing under WIC 252. Opened San Diego form D-204: 'all parties to the case must agree that the commissioner can act as a temporary judge.' Justia is a reprint, not the official constitution site (leginfo would not load).

title: Group Home
statement: Un hogar donde varios jóvenes de crianza viven juntos con personal pagado en lugar de una familia de crianza. California ha pasado la mayor parte del cuidado en grupo de jóvenes de crianza a programas residenciales terapéuticos de corto plazo (STRTP). Todavía existen algunos hogares de grupo.
source_name: Legislative Analyst's Office report, Feb. 23, 2021; CDSS Children's Residential Facility Information page
source_says: Short-Term Therapeutic Programs Replace Group Homes. ... The deadline for group homes to convert to STRTPs was the end of December 2020.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 9dc6bb35). Searched 'Continuum of Care Reform CDSS group homes short-term residential therapeutic programs replace group home'. CDSS issue brief and ACL 17-122 would not load (robots block). Opened the LAO report: 'a key goal of CCR is to end group homes as a placement option for foster youth.' For 'some group homes still exist' searched 'CDSS Community Care Licensing children's residential facility types group home', opened https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/childrens-residential/resources-for-providers/facility-information: Group Home (GH) is still a listed license type that 'provides 24-hour non-medical care and supervision to children', next to STRTP. WIC 11400(h) on public.law still defines 'group home'.

title: Legal Guardianship
source_says: The court shall also make an order for visitation with the parents or guardians unless the court finds by a preponderance of the evidence that the visitation would be detrimental
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (source, id b5dd7f9b). Searched 'public.law WIC 366.24 tribal customary adoption' which returned 366.26 and 366.3; opened both. 366.26(b)(3) 'Appoint a relative or relatives with whom the child is currently residing as legal guardian'; (c)(4)(A) caretakers 'shall become legal guardians' where ending parental rights is not in the child's best interest. 366.3 (https://california.public.law/codes/welfare_and_institutions_code_section_366.3): (b)(2) 'proceedings to terminate a legal guardianship'; (b)(3) 'Unless the parental rights of the child's parent or parents have been terminated, the parents shall be notified' and services may again be ordered. Both sections support the entry.

title: No Contest Plea
statement: Si usted declara que no disputa, renuncia a su derecho a un juicio sobre la petición. Luego el juez decide si la petición es verdadera y puede usar el informe del trabajador social para decidir.
source_name: Form JV-190 items 4, 5a; Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.682(d), (e); WIC 355(b)
source_says: I understand that if I plead no contest or submit the petition on the report, the court will probably find that the petition is true.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id cb3142d5). Searched 'JV-190 Waiver of Rights Juvenile Dependency no contest', opened the form: item 4, by 'pleading no contest, I am giving up the following rights' including 'The right to a trial or hearing.' Opened rule 5.682 on courts.ca.gov: (d) parent may 'plead no contest and waive further jurisdictional hearing'; (e) court finds waiver of 'the right to a trial on the issues' and whether 'allegations of the petition as admitted are true as alleged'. Opened WIC 355 on public.law: (b) 'A social study prepared by the petitioning agency ... constitutes competent evidence upon which a finding of jurisdiction pursuant to Section 300 may be based'.

title: Noncustodial Parent
statement: . Si ese padre viene a la corte y no puede pagar un abogado, puede pedirle al juez que le dé uno.
source_name: WIC 317(a)(1), (b); California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: When it appears to the court that a parent or guardian of the child desires counsel but is presently financially unable to afford and cannot for that reason employ counsel
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id dd33799c). Searched 'WIC 317 desires counsel but is presently financially unable to afford', opened public.law WIC 317: (a)(1) as quoted; (b) 'the court shall appoint counsel for the parent or guardian, unless the court finds that the parent or guardian has made a knowing and intelligent waiver'. Opened selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/juvenile-dependency/guide-parents: 'The judge will also assign a lawyer to the other parent of your child' and 'If you cannot afford a lawyer, the judge will assign one to you.'

title: Notice
statement: El mensaje oficial que le dice la fecha, la hora y el lugar de una audiencia y de qué se trata. Normalmente es en papel. Para la primera audiencia, el trabajador social puede decírselo de palabra.
source_name: WIC 290.1 (opening paragraph, (d), (e)); Judicial Council booklet
source_says: The probation officer or social worker shall serve notice as prescribed in this section. ... Service of the notice shall be written or oral.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id ba71591e). Searched 'public.law WIC 315 detention hearing', which returned WIC 290.1; opened it twice. (d)(1) notice of the initial petition hearing includes 'The date, time, and place of the hearing' plus a copy of the petition; (e) written or oral, and 'If the person being served cannot read, notice shall be given orally.' For 'usually on paper' opened the booklet: 'you will be mailed a paper that tells you when and where you need to go.'

title: Notice
statement: . Si se muda, dele su nueva dirección por escrito al secretario de la corte o a su trabajador social. Dígale también a su abogado.
source_name: Form JV-140, Notification of Mailing Address; Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(i)
source_says: Notice of the new mailing address must be provided in writing.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id ba71591e). Searched 'WIC 316.1 permanent mailing address notifies the court or the social services agency of a new mailing address in writing', opened form JV-140 on courts.ca.gov: notices go to the address given 'until and unless you notify the court or the social worker or probation officer on your case of your new mailing address.' Also opened rule 5.534(i): address is used 'until and unless the parent or guardian, or the attorney of record ... submits written notification of a change of mailing address'. Booklet: 'it is very important that you tell the judge or court clerk your new address'.

title: Notice
statement: The message that tells you when and where your hearing is. It is usually a letter, but for the first hearing the social worker may just tell you.
source_name: WIC 290.1(d), (e); Judicial Council booklet
source_says: Service of the notice shall be written or oral.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id ba71591e). Same pages as the definition record: WIC 290.1 covers notice of the initial petition hearing, served by 'The probation officer or social worker', with 'The date, time, and place of the hearing'. Booklet: 'you will be mailed a paper that tells you when and where you need to go.'

title: Party
statement: WIC §317.5(b); Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534; Judicial Council, Juvenile Dependency Court and You
source_name: WIC 317.5(b); Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.534(e), (j)(4); Judicial Council booklet
source_says: Each minor who is the subject of a dependency proceeding is a party to that proceeding.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (source, id 30c2e8e6). Searched 'public.law WIC 317.5 is a party to that proceeding', opened the page. Opened rule 5.534 on courts.ca.gov three times: (e) 'The tribe of an Indian child is entitled to intervene as a party at any stage of a dependency proceeding'; (j)(4) lists 'all legal parties to the action', and that list includes 'the social services agency', 'any parent' and 'the child'. Opened the booklet: 'you may hear the legal term that the tribe is a party to the case.' Rule 5.534 is the right rule for this entry; the pinpoint for parents and the agency is (j)(4).

title: Permanency Hearing
statement: Una audiencia que se hace a más tardar 12 meses después de que su hijo entró en cuidado de crianza. Si el juez le da más tiempo, hay una audiencia más dentro de los 18 meses desde el día en que sacaron a su hijo de su hogar.
source_says: The permanency hearing shall be held no later than 12 months after the date the child entered foster care
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id ea30de18). Searched 'public.law WIC 366.21 permanency hearing no later than 12 months; 366.22 within 18 months', opened both. 366.21(g)(1): 'Continue the case for up to 6 months for a permanency review hearing, provided that the hearing shall occur within 18 months of the date the child was originally taken from the physical custody of their parent'. 366.22(a)(1) (https://california.public.law/codes/ca_welf_and_inst_code_section_366.22): 'shall occur within 18 months after the date the child was originally removed'.

title: Permanency Hearing
statement: The hearing at 12 months where the judge decides if your child can come home. If the judge gives more time, there is one more by 18 months.
source_says: the court shall order the return of the child to the physical custody of their parent or legal guardian unless the court finds, by a preponderance of the evidence
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id ea30de18). Same pages as the definition record. 366.21(f)(1) sets the 12-month hearing and the return decision; (g)(1) and 366.22(a)(1) set the further hearing 'within 18 months' when the case is continued.

title: Reasonable Efforts
statement: La ley dice que el condado debe hacer esfuerzos razonables para que un niño se quede seguro en su hogar. En la mayoría de los casos también debe tratar de ayudar a la familia a reunirse otra vez. En algunos casos graves, el juez puede decidir que el condado no tiene que ofrecer esa ayuda.
source_says: The court shall make a determination as to whether reasonable efforts were made to prevent or to eliminate the need for removal of the minor from their home
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 2fd64c4a). Searched 'public.law WIC 224.1 Indian child active efforts', which returned WIC 361; opened it and read (e). For the reunification sentences opened WIC 361.5 on public.law: (a) 'the juvenile court shall order the social worker to provide child welfare services'; (b) 'Reunification services need not be provided to a parent or guardian described in this subdivision when the court finds, by clear and convincing evidence, any of the following'.

title: Reasonable Efforts
statement: The county has to really try to keep families together. In most cases it also has to help them get back together.
source_says: Reunification services need not be provided to a parent or guardian described in this subdivision ... when the court finds, by clear and convincing evidence, any of the following
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id 2fd64c4a). Same pages as the definition record: WIC 361(e) (reasonable efforts to prevent removal) and WIC 361.5(a) (court 'shall order the social worker to provide child welfare services') with the (b) exceptions, which is why 'in most cases' is right.

title: Service Provider
statement: Su trabajador social puede preguntarles a sus proveedores cómo le va a usted y decírselo al juez.
source_name: WIC 366.21(c), (e)(1), (f)(1)(C); Orange County Social Services Agency policy E-0105
source_says: making monthly telephonic, written, or in-person contact with each service provider
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 405f92be). The booklet cited by the entry does not cover this (checked twice). Searched for county monitored visit policy, which returned Orange County policy E-0105; opened it: social worker contacts each service provider monthly and documents 'significant information related to the progress of the case'. For 'tell the judge' opened WIC 366.21 on public.law: the social worker's report covers 'services provided or offered' and 'the progress made', and the court weighs 'the efforts or progress, or both, demonstrated by the parent'. The county policy is one county's practice, which fits the entry's 'may'.

title: Supervised Visit
statement: Las visitas pueden ser supervisadas al principio.
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy, Family Time; Judicial Council booklet
source_says: a gradual means of decreasing the level of supervision, from supervised to unsupervised
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 3a62220e). Opened the booklet: only says a parent can ask to 'change your supervised visits to unsupervised visits.' Searched 'county child welfare policy monitored visits who may monitor', opened the L.A. County DCFS Family Time policy: 'there is a gradual reduction in supervision, if visits were supervised'; before disposition visits 'may not be supervised unless the court has ordered supervision'. Both fit 'may be supervised at first'; neither says visits always start supervised.

title: THP
statement: CDSS Transitional Housing Programs page; WIC §16522 (licensing rule only)
source_name: CDSS Transitional Housing Programs page; WIC 16522
source_says: provides current and former foster youth additional supports they need to successfully transition to independence.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (source, id 507fef3d). Searched 'CDSS Transitional Housing Programs THPP THP-NMD THP-Plus', opened the CDSS page: THP-NMD is 'a supervised, supportive housing program for young adults (ages 18-21)'; THP-Plus serves 'young adults who exited foster care'. Searched 'public.law WIC 16522 transitional housing placement providers', opened https://california.public.law/codes/welfare_and_institutions_code_section_16522: 'The State Department of Social Services shall license transitional housing placement providers'. So the CDSS page supports the definition and 16522 is a licensing rule, as the citation says.

title: Visit Monitor
statement: Puede ser un trabajador social, otro trabajador del condado, un monitor pagado, la persona que cuida a su hijo, o un pariente o amigo que el condado apruebe.
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy, Family Time
source_says: The child's caregiver may also monitor the visit, provided there are no safety concerns.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 45bc3a86). Searched 'county child welfare policy monitored visits who may monitor relative caregiver professional monitor', opened the L.A. County DCFS Family Time policy. Monitors listed: 'A CSW, SCSW, ARA or any staff whose job description includes provision of family time supervision'; 'Any person paid for providing supervised family time services'; caregiver; 'Family friend or relative agreed to by all parties, with whom the child is comfortable' (worker consults a supervisor 'prior to approval'). Notes: 'All family time needs to be documented in the Contact Notebook, including any report back from a Monitor.' This is one county's policy; other counties were not opened, and the entry says 'may'.

title: Visit Monitor
statement: County visiting policy and the judge's visiting order
source_name: Los Angeles County DCFS policy, Family Time (one example of a county visiting policy)
source_says: Select a Monitor based on the court's orders and FTP. ... the court makes the final decision as to the manner in which supervision is provided
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (source, id 45bc3a86). The citation names no single document, so it cannot be opened as written. Opened one county policy as a test (L.A. County DCFS Family Time): it shows the monitor is set by county policy and the court's order, and it lists each kind of monitor in the entry. Only one of 58 counties was checked. Naming this policy as an example in the citation would let a reader retrace it.

title: Voluntary Declaration of Parentage
statement: . Una vez que se presenta ante el estado, convierte a una persona en padre legal del niño.
source_name: Family Code 7573(c), (d)
source_says: a voluntary declaration of parentage takes effect on the filing of the document with the Department of Child Support Services.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 44f7d18e). Searched 'public.law Family Code 7573 voluntary declaration of parentage filed with the Department of Child Support Services', opened the page twice. (d): a completed declaration 'that has been filed with the Department of Child Support Services is equivalent to a judgment of parentage of the child and confers on the declarant all rights and duties of a parent', with listed exceptions.

title: Voluntary Declaration of Parentage
statement: A form parents sign that makes someone the legal parent once it is filed with the state.
source_name: Family Code 7573(c), (d)
source_says: is equivalent to a judgment of parentage of the child and confers on the declarant all rights and duties of a parent.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (simple_text, id 44f7d18e). Same page as the definition record: (c) takes effect 'on the filing of the document with the Department of Child Support Services'; (d) filed declaration equals a judgment of parentage.

title: Voluntary Services
statement: . El niño puede quedarse en casa mientras la familia recibe ayuda. Un padre también puede aceptar una colocación corta fuera del hogar.
source_says: An out-of-home placement of a minor without adjudication by the juvenile court may occur only when ... There is a mutual decision between the child's parent, Indian custodian, or guardian
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id b9620f0b). Searched 'WIC 301 in lieu of filing a petition program of supervision; voluntary placement agreement 180 days 16507.4', opened WIC 301 on public.law ('in lieu of filing a petition ... and with consent of the child's parent or guardian, undertake a program of supervision of the child'; (c) names 'a voluntary family maintenance program'). Opened 16507.4 (written agreement 'specifying the terms of the voluntary placement'). For 'short' opened https://california.public.law/codes/ca_welf_and_inst_code_section_16507.3: 'shall be limited to a period not to exceed 180 days.' Sacramento court terms: services 'to prevent the removal of a child from the home.'

title: Writ Petition
statement: El juez debe informarle sobre este recurso cuando se fija la audiencia .26. Si usted no estuvo en la corte, el secretario le envía un aviso por correo. No espere a que le avisen. Dígale a su abogado de inmediato que quiere presentarlo. Si se le pasa el plazo, pierde el derecho de apelar esa orden.
source_name: WIC 366.26(l)(1)-(3); Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.590(b)
source_says: The advisement must be given orally to those present when the court orders the hearing under section 366.26.
steps: Live text confirmed by SELECT (definition, id 42177a8d). Searched 'rule 5.590 advisement extraordinary writ order setting 366.26 hearing clerk first-class mail', opened rule 5.590(b): if a party is not present, 'the advisement must be made by the clerk of the court by first-class mail to the last known address of the party or by electronic service'. Opened WIC 366.26 on public.law: (l)(1) the setting order 'is not appealable at any time' unless 'A petition for extraordinary writ review was filed in a timely manner'; (l)(2) failure to file 'shall preclude subsequent review by appeal'; (l)(3)(A) court 'shall advise all parties of the requirement'.
